newsitem.title: USA: LIPA close to deal for Lilco - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: LIPA close to deal for Lilco - WSJ.

text.p: The Long Island Power Authority's deal to acquire most of Long Island Lighting Co's assets could be announced as soon as next week, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
When Brooklyn Union Gas Co announced plans to merge with Lilco after Christmas, LIPA Chairman Frank Zarb said there would be an agreement in six weeks, spokesmen for both noted.
Officially, both declined to comment, citing ongoing negotiations.
Bond traders felt the Journal report adds credence to rumors of progress in talks.
Lilco's long bonds continue to tighten, adding 15 to 20 basis points in early Monday trading.
"We expect to hear something soon," a Lilco spokeswoman said.

LIPA officials were not immediately available to comment on the report, which said LIPA has agreed to pay about $5 billion, including $4 billion for the regulatory asset created when the state mothballed the Shoreham nuclear power plant.

If the transaction goes through as planned, Lilco would be split in two, with the natural gas distribution and power generation businesses becoming part of the merger proposed by Brooklyn Union, the newspaper said.
One utility official said the numbers sound accurate.
Citing people familiar with the talks, the Journal said lawyers and bankers for Lilco and Brooklyn Union are working out adjustments to what had been a $25 per share price to be paid for Lilco stock.
It said the merged Lilco/Brooklyn Union is expected to sign a contract to operate the LIPA-owned power transmission and distribution business for six to eight years.

The newspaper said a private-letter ruling is being sought from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service that would assure the $5 billion in municipal bonds issued to finance the transaction would be tax-free and that Lilco would avoid a $2 billion capital gains tax on the asset transfers to a government entity. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
